top_story: A Washington-brokered framework agreement signed by لبنان and Israel on 26 June marks the clearest diplomatic effort to contain one front of the regional war, but it unfolded against sharper escalation in the Gulf. After Iran rejected a UN-backed plan on 25 June to free ships trapped in the Strait of Hormuz and shipping continued to use the Oman passage despite Iranian warnings, a cargo vessel was struck and US forces responded hours later with strikes on Iranian missile, drone, and coastal radar sites. This sequence shows maritime coercion around Hormuz overtaking de-escalation elsewhere, tightening pressure on trade flows, coastal communities, and already strained civilian economies. The immediate regional picture is a split one: localized diplomacy is advancing on the Israel-Lebanon front even as direct US-Iran confrontation threatens to broaden the conflict.
